```

After creating a Node, the user has a few responsibilities:

First, read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step 2.

1. Write Entries, HardState and Snapshot to persistent storage in order, i.e. Entries first, then HardState and Snapshot if they are not empty. If persistent storage supports atomic writes then all of them can be written together. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk, and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be large). Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important to make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling. The easiest way to achieve this is to serialise the messages directly inside the main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine. If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange() to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange (but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates. This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage type can be used for this (if repopulating its state upon a restart), or a custom disk-backed implementation can be supplied.

Third, after receiving a message from another node, pass it to Node.Step:

```go
	func recvRaftRPC(ctx context.Context, m raftpb.Message) {
		n.Step(ctx, m)
	}
```

Finally, call `Node.Tick()` at regular intervals (probably via a `time.Ticker`). Raft has two important timeouts: heartbeat and the election timeout. However, internally to the raft package time is represented by an abstract "tick".

    select {
    case <-s.Ticker:
      n.Tick()
    case rd := <-s.Node.Ready():

items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact 3a14b92a84ad47ddaaf66107babcb3b9 version 1 against O-auto-exit version 1 and execution c14ff92624034255a3f506d0795b2631. Applicability comes from tracker.Config automatic transition when possible, contrasted with manual explicit joint mode, and ConfChangeV2 implicit-mode selection. The driver uses real public RawNode bootstrap, campaign, proposal, Step, Ready, ApplyConfChange and Advance; it assigns no protocol fields. The actual entry at index 5 removes node 3 using implicit joint consensus, while node 1 and node 2 remain voters. It starts transfer after applying that entry but before acknowledging its Ready. This serialized interleaving is permitted by RawNode and is also representable in Node.run while waiting for Advance. Persistence precedes outgoing delivery; every committed entry is processed before Advance, and the no-crash MemoryStorage substitution is explicit. Only TimeoutNow is lost; the actual trace contains one such drop before cancellation. Removed-peer replies are logged admission rejections, not suppressed results.

The monitor has one unique cycle_admitted prerequisite and one cycle_result for the stable independent identity (case, operation, leader, joint_index). The admission reports live AutoLeave true, three outgoing voters, leader state and transfer zero with queues empty. The result retains actual full state before/after, not an expected result. Independently reassembled Go output by test stream and parsed the complete JSON records; the two captured states compare equal. The implication repeat_cycle => !joint_pending is false because both repeat_cycle and joint_pending are true. This is a closed-cycle witness for the automatic-continuation obligation, not an assertion that 30 ticks is a deadline. The test stops after fixed work independently of the property. The source history and configuration_applied records establish the same joint entry and transfer producer; no constructed peer response substitutes for it.

State coverage includes all RawNode fields, all raft fields except logging sinks, reachable log/unstable and MemoryStorage bytes, membership and progress/inflight state, pending reads, deferred replies and stepsOnAdvance. At both endpoints all three logs have committed=applying=applied=5, unstable entries/snapshot empty, application size zero and stable offset 6. Leader Match for all peers is 5 with no outstanding inflights; messages and transport are empty. All nodes retain term 2, followers have electionElapsed zero, and leader has both clocks zero. Capture excludes MemoryStorage.callStats: their source uses only increment diagnostic access counters, never decision inputs. Logging sinks do not control this normal path; tracing is disabled by the build-selected nop implementation. Slice capacity and pointer addresses are allocation details on this suffix; live contents, nilness and field structure are retained, and the same node instances/closure receivers persist.

The repeating schedule ticks all three nodes once then drains all Ready and FIFO transport; sorted tracker.Visit makes broadcasts deterministic. Each follower's tick reaches elapsed 1, below its captured randomized timeout (17 or 18), and the delivered heartbeat resets it to zero. Leader heartbeats recur every tick and CheckQuorum every ten; responses keep both joint majorities active. The leader's captured randomized timeout is 14 but is not used by tickHeartbeat. No role reset occurs on this suffix, so the only random producer, resetRandomizedElectionTimeout, is not called. There are no read requests, stale replies, snapshots or storage callbacks left to alter future transitions. Ordinary heartbeat Readys contain no committed entries, so Advance schedules no appliedTo retry. abortLeaderTransfer clears the target but schedules no exit. Thus repetition can continue under complete required service without unrelated proposals or forced elections.

The no-transfer control exits at index 6. The diagnostic proposal after the measured suffix commits an ordinary entry at 6 and an automatic exit at 7. These are contrary evidence to broad unavailability, but corroborate that the joint quorum works and application progress supplies the missing trigger. Exported Status.Config.AutoLeave is false because Clone omits it; the checker deliberately reads live tracker state and the full capture, so it does not confuse that separate reporting discrepancy with loss of the live mode. No issue found in correspondence for this scoped witness; wider scheduling and safety claims are not established.

Reviewed fixed artifact 839792d838e7490b8ad130b505d3a87c version 1, obligation O-read-singleton version 1, and execution 637a23bb7ef346fbbfb558fc4d9e6f6a. Applicability is the independently grounded support duty: ReadOnlySafe obtains read authority through a quorum, and MajorityConfig counts configured voters only. The singleton shortcut can substitute local support for communication only when the local responder is the singleton voter. IsSingleton documentation assumes that voter is the leader, but its implementation checks only set cardinalities. switchToConfig explicitly permits a removed node to remain leader when StepDownOnRemoval is false. This option controls stepping down, not a documented exception to ReadOnlySafe. Captured caller/API instructions require ordered configuration application but state no prohibition on ReadIndex after removal or unconditional requirement to stop the RawNode. Thus optional immediate step-down is a protection, not a prerequisite silently imposed on the false-mode case.

The fixed driver uses actual public bootstrap, election, proposal, committed self-removal, Ready persistence/application and Advance. Node 1 and node 2 both apply removal at index 5 and install voters [2]. The driver then partitions peer communication; node 2 legitimately elects itself as the singleton and applies a new ordinary entry at index 7, term 3. Only then does the caller request a unique ReadIndex context from node 1. No state, term, quorum acknowledgment or role is assigned by the harness. MemoryStorage is explicit no-crash persistence; every outbound message is detached after persistence, and no concurrent RawNode operation exists. No tick-based deadline is used: these operations fit within an interval between caller ticks, and the safety comparison concerns the immediate returned barrier.

The result is not an assumed expected value. The harness counts actual Ready.ReadStates matching node 1 and the fresh context. It computes eligible local singleton support from the observed installed voter sets; this is the exact necessary condition under the zero-communication scope. The delivery counter increments only at an actual peer Step boundary after request start. Since all peer messages are dropped under the explicit partition and queues are drained, there is no hidden quorum response or pending delivery. The result event is emitted after bounded driver drain in both cases, independent of whether ReadState exists. Its admission_alias selects read_admitted; identity (step_down, operation, node, context) uniquely joins each admission and result. No compared membership/support value is used as an identity or applicability filter. The only result applicability check is independently required zero peer delivery. Both operations meet it, and all records parse completely.

In the false-option case, read_returned=true, response_count=1 and index=5, while peer_messages_delivered=0, voters=[2], self_voter=false and local_singleton_support=false. Therefore read_returned implies local_singleton_support is violated. In the true-option control, read_returned=false with response_count=0; the implication holds without demanding eventual response or asserting a successful read. Both final Ready queues are empty. The measured quorum-eligibility failure is narrower than a stale client-read claim: application index on node 1 is 5, equal to the returned read index, and the documented further-than/greater-than wait is not shown satisfied. The stored old application value is diagnostic only, not an asserted client result. The earlier node 2 write demonstrates the authority transition history and potential significance, but is not used to weaken that endpoint requirement.

Source cause and measured scope agree: retained StateLeader dispatch reaches the cardinality-only singleton branch and produces responseToReadIndexReq before the multi-voter current-term/quorum path. The Status copy defect affects AutoLeave only; voter maps used here are copied explicitly and agree with actual applied configuration at both nodes.
